about: The fish species' own ID marks, adults only: agent drafts until Pierre validates them (ROADMAP "Fish sheets at three levels": the writing as agent drafts marked as drafts, families first, then genera, then species; Pierre, 2026-11-19: "Est-ce qu'on a seulement fait le même travail pour les adultes?"). For every game species (the species of every teaching node of fish.json): 1 to 3 marks that tell it from the other game species of its genus by eye on a photo, in our own words, short (at most 80 characters), with no number (a count is never a photo cue); a species named in a mark is one of its genus's game species (rules C3, C6). Written from public pages read on 2026-11-19: FishBase species summaries (fb-, fbm- its morphology page), Fishes of Australia (foa-, the page id), Reef Life Survey (rls-, the page slug). src: each source {t, u}, t starting with the source's short name before its first comma. species, by the scientific name fish.json shows: marks, each [words, refs], a ref [src key, the words of the page it rests on, verbatim: each was checked by script against the page text as read]; look (kept here, not shown yet): the look-alikes a source names, each [species, refs], only species of fish.json confirmed in the Philippines (rule C6: present.ph); ease (kept here, not shown yet): a source's words on how easy or hard it is to tell, [src key, its words]. none: a game species left without marks and why, never a mark guessed. draft: true while Pierre has not validated them: the build marks every species' marks as a draft (fish.json mdraft), which the species sheet says. tools/build_fish.py add_families (species_marks) puts marks, msrc, mby and mdraft on fish.json species and stops on anything else; learn.js marksBox shows them on the species sheet as it shows a genus's.
